focus: Apply-response with nil apply_response_template_subject (legacy job) — does the full chain handle it?

observations.title: Migration does not backfill apply_response_template_subject for existing jobs
observations.description: The migration (20260603212057) adds apply_response_template_subject as a nullable string column with no default and no data migration. All existing jobs in production will have nil for this column after migration. Only newly created jobs receive the default '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}' via add_default_apply_response_template. This is correctly handled by the fallback chain but worth noting.

observations.title: Cypress seeder does not set apply_response_template_subject (simulates legacy)
observations.description: The Cypress job seeder appears to skip add_default_apply_response_template, so seeded jobs have apply_response_template_subject=nil. This actually serves as a realistic test scenario for legacy jobs.

summary: All 18 tests passed. The full chain correctly handles legacy jobs with nil apply_response_template_subject. parse_apply_response_text(nil) returns '', ChannelMessage is created with subject='', and the mailer fallback at line 116 of channel_message_mailer.rb produces the correct default subject '<job_title> at <org_name>'. Both the JobApplication model path and the CustomerApi::CompleteJobApplication interactor path are verified. No bugs found.
